focus: (1) simpler, shorter, more correct, in the author's voice; (2) plain-language summary of each derivation; (3) reorganization

findings.finding: Per-derivation simplifications and summaries; reorganize: merge Sec. 2 with Sec. 3.4 (map, inverse, drift together); merge Apps. A+B, D+E; split App. C into dispersion/overstability and empirical instabilities; add Limitations section.
findings.comment: Simplifications for App. A, the (10) O(ei) clause, Sec. 2.2's frequency identity, and B/C framing are right. Merging Sec. 3.4 into Sec. 2 is reasonable (the drift is Sec. 2's map run forward). A separate Limitations section is premature in a draft whose introduction and summary are placeholders. Reorganization put to the author.

findings.finding: The steady solution does not tend to h_forced on the wave side; Appendix E shows the wave grows as sigma^(-1/2). Only the finite-time limit does.
findings.comment: Right; Appendix E itself says so (line 1136 'at any fixed x > 0' and its last paragraph), but the abstract and Sec. 4.1.2 flatten it. Same as grok-4.
findings.fix: done 2026-11-24: state the finite-time limit in the abstract and Sec. 4.1.2

findings.where: Sec. 3.4 'second-order symplectic' and 'exact for the unperturbed motion'
findings.finding: Exact invertibility does not establish symplecticity; the drift is exact for Eqns. (inplane),(zvz), which are themselves first order.
findings.comment: 'Exact for the unperturbed motion of Eqns. (...)' is literally true and already names the first-order equations, but a reader can take it as exact Keplerian/J2 motion. 'Symplectic' is inherited from H25's description of the MERCURY scheme; the epicyclic drift is not shown to be a canonical map here. Drop 'symplectic' or attribute it, and say the drift is exact for the first-order epicyclic motion.
findings.fix: done 2026-11-24: 'exact' reworded; 'symplectic' kept at the author's request, as in hahn13 and hahn25 and as the scheme's family is usually described

findings.finding: Numbers behind the macros were not supplied, so cannot be audited.
findings.comment: An artifact of what was sent, not a paper problem: every macro is computed from the run outputs by tools/paper_numbers.py (CLAUDE.md rule), and the notebooks reproduce each figure. No change to the paper.

findings.finding: Paragraph says the potential 'exerts the torque T on the simulated ring' and then 'the ring does not feel this torque'. T is a reconstructed diagnostic.
findings.comment: All three reviewers found it (gemini-7, grok-2). The kick is only A_z (Eqn. vres_force), so T is the torque the resonant potential would exert; it tests amplitude and phase. Rewrite as a diagnostic. Applying the azimuthal force as a real test is a possible later run, not part of this revision.
findings.fix: done 2026-11-24: rewrite paragraph and Fig. torque caption

findings.where: Sec. 4.1.3 'what free motion remains averages away over time'
findings.finding: Averaging the positive inclination does not cancel free motion; B11 says the free part never decays.
findings.comment: Free motion is small because the turn-on is slow, not because it averages away. Same point as gemini-4's first source.

findings.finding: The code's i = [(z/a)^2 + (v_z/a nu)^2]^(1/2) is not |h|/a when omega_m != nu_a (B20); the O(x) residual is partly that.
findings.comment: B20 in notes/equations.md quantifies it (0.15% with exact D vs up to 3.6% with Eqn. vres_inc). One clause naming both O(x) sources. Same as gemini-4, grok-5.

findings.where: App. C 'should be run with R <~ 0.1, viscous or not'
findings.finding: A few runs of one ringlet do not make R <~ 0.1 a general rule; the sawtooth grows at R = 0.
findings.comment: Same as grok-3. Present 0.1 as advice for the tested ringlet and separate it from the open sawtooth problem.

findings.comment: Same as gemini-6, grok-8. Label it an estimate and drop 'only by a narrower ringlet' until derived.

findings.comment: All three. Soften to 'in the sense the lattice predicts' now; overlaying B13 on the figure would need B13 to be presented in the paper (T24), a larger change for the author to decide.
findings.fix: done 2026-11-24: lattice dispersion |D| = X(k Delta) (P9) quoted for all three runs; the remainder attributed to the finite width

findings.fix: done 2026-11-24: narrow wording; tests are an author decision

findings.comment: Real and already open in notes/phase2/streamline_gravity.md: lambda = m1 Omega_a/(2 pi v) underestimates lambda's variation along an m >= 2 streamline by about m. State the estimator and why it is minor for tightly wound waves (|k|r >> m), as gemini-6 suggests; fixing the estimator is a code change for later.
findings.fix: done 2026-11-24: state estimator and its limit

findings.finding: GT79 readers expect the satellite to add angular momentum to the ring at an inner Lindblad resonance; the negative sign may be an error.
findings.comment: At an inner Lindblad (or vertical) resonance the exterior satellite removes angular momentum from the ring (GT79: the satellite repels the ring; ring edges are pushed inward), so T < 0 is right, and the simulated torque settles onto T_L with that sign. Saying in words what T < 0 means is worthwhile, with an equation-level citation (grok-12).
